article_title: Engagement Matters: Student Perceptions on the Importance of Engagement  Strategies in the Online Learning Environment
citation: Martin, F., & Bolliger, D. U. (2018). Engagement Matters: Student Perceptions on the Importance of Engagement Strategies in the Online Learning Environment. Online Learning, 22(1). https://doi.org/10.24059/olj.v22i1.1092
title: 38-item engagement strategies survey instrument
description: A survey instrument used to collect student perceptions of engagement strategies in online courses. As the article reports, "One hundred and fifty five students completed a 38-item survey on learner-to-learner, learner-to-instructor, and learner-to-content engagement strategies." The items are organized by Moore's three interaction types and ask students to rate the benefit of specific strategies such as icebreaker discussions, announcements, rubrics, and real-world projects.
requirements: Respondents must have experience as students in online courses to rate the strategies
target_learning_goals: evaluating engagement strategies in online courses
examples: Completed by 155 students to identify the most beneficial strategies in each of the three interaction categories.
key_sources: Martin, F., & Bolliger, D. U. (2018). Engagement Matters: Student Perceptions on the Importance of Engagement Strategies in the Online Learning Environment. Online Learning, 22(1). https://doi.org/10.24059/olj.v22i1.1092

article_title: The effectiveness of problem-based learning in gynecology and obstetrics education in China: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
citation: Bi S, Liu R, Li J, Gu J. (2021). The effectiveness of problem-based learning in gynecology and obstetrics education in China: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000024660
title: Pool of 38 randomized controlled trials comparing PBL with traditional teaching in Chinese gynecology and obstetrics education
description: The evidence base for this meta-analysis is a pool of randomized controlled trials published in Chinese between 2015 and 2020 comparing PBL with traditional teaching in obstetrics and gynecology courses. As the article states, "a total of 38 controlled studies with 1494 participants in the PBL group and 1511 participants in traditional teaching groups were included for this meta-analysis." Sample sizes ranged from 31 to 218 with a median of 71, mostly interns. Only studies with duration longer than 6 months were included in the meta-analysis.
requirements: Studies had to be randomized controlled trials comparing PBL with traditional teaching in Chinese obstetrics and gynecology education with usable outcome data
constraints: All included trials had unclear bias for blinding of participants, personnel, and outcome assessment; 16 studies were ambiguous about random sequence generation
examples: The search screened 519 records from Chinese and English databases and included 38 trials published 2015-2020, all in Chinese.
key_sources: Bi S, Liu R, Li J, Gu J. (2021). The effectiveness of problem-based learning in gynecology and obstetrics education in China: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000024660

article_title: The performance of ChatGPT on medical image-based assessments and implications for medical education.
citation: Xiang Y, Wei C. (2025). The performance of ChatGPT on medical image-based assessments and implications for medical education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07752-0
title: Set of 38 publicly available image-based USMLE Step 1 and Step 2 CK sample questions spanning 18 medical disciplines
description: This element is the item set the study assembled: all publicly available USMLE-style multiple-choice questions with image content from the NBME/FSMB Step 1 and Step 2 CK sample materials. "A total of 38 image-based questions spanning multiple medical disciplines—including dermatology, cardiology, and gastroenterology—were included in the analysis." The items were grouped into 18 distinct medical disciplines, with dermatology the largest category (6 questions), followed by cardiology and gastroenterology (4 each). Each item combined an image with accompanying text in standard examination format.
requirements: Items must combine an image with accompanying textual information in standard USMLE examination format
constraints: The article notes the relatively small number of publicly available image-based USMLE-style questions (n = 38) limited statistical power and generalizability
target_learners: Medical students and licensing examination candidates
target_learning_goals: Clinical knowledge for diagnosis and management (Step 2 CK)
examples: The 38 image-based items were administered once per model via the ChatGPT web interface with a fixed answer-only prompt, and correctness was scored against the official sample-item answer key
key_sources: Xiang Y, Wei C. (2025). The performance of ChatGPT on medical image-based assessments and implications for medical education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07752-0
